# Migrate to Azure Blob Storage

@include "@global/vagrant-eol.mdx"

This guide walks you through moving your Vagrant boxes from HCP Vagrant Registry
to Azure Blob Storage and referencing them from a Vagrantfile. Using the
Microsoft Azure command line interface (CLI), you create a storage account, add a
container, upload your boxes, and optionally serve them publicly.

## Overview

Azure Blob Storage organizes data in a hierarchy. At the top sits a storage
account, which can hold many containers. Each container, in turn, can hold
virtually any number of blobs, such as your `vagrant.box` files. In this guide,
you create a single storage account, add one container to it, and upload your
boxes into that container as blobs.

## Cost considerations

Azure Blob Storage is a paid service, so review the pricing model before you
migrate your boxes to understand the charges you may incur. Billing spans several
dimensions:

- **Storage.** You pay for the amount of data you store, charged per gigabyte per
  month. The rate depends on the access tier you choose, such as Hot or Cool.
- **Operations.** You pay for operations against your blobs, including the write
  operations you make when you upload boxes and the read operations Vagrant makes
  when it downloads them.
- **Data transfer.** You pay for data transferred out of Azure to the internet,
  such as when users download boxes from a public container. Inbound transfers
  into Azure are typically free, but check the pricing page for the most current
  details.

New Azure accounts include a free allowance of storage, operations, and data
transfer for a limited time. For current rates, refer to the
[Azure Blob Storage pricing page](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/storage/blobs/).
To estimate your costs, use the
[Azure pricing calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator/).

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, complete the following:

- Download the boxes you want to migrate from HCP Vagrant Registry so that you
  have the `vagrant.box` files available locally.
- Create an [Azure account](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/).

## Install the Azure CLI

Install the Azure CLI by following the
[Azure CLI installation guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli).

## Log in

Log in to Azure:

```shell-session
$ az login
```

The login command supports many additional options, such as service principal
and managed identity authentication. Refer to the
[az login reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/reference-index#az-login)
for the full list.

## Create a resource group

A storage account needs a resource group to live in, so create one first. Set the
`--location` value to a Region near you or your users, such as `eastus`:

```shell-session
$ az group create --name GROUP_NAME --location LOCATION
```

To see the Regions available to your account, list them first:

```shell-session
$ az account list-locations --output table
```

## Create a storage account

With the resource group in place, create a storage account inside it:

```shell-session
$ az storage account create --name ACCOUNT_NAME --resource-group GROUP_NAME --location LOCATION --sku Standard_LRS
```

Storage account names must be globally unique across all of Azure and can contain
only lowercase letters and numbers. The `--sku` value sets the redundancy option;
for instance, `Standard_LRS` maintains three copies of the data within a single
Region. For the complete list of options, refer to
[az storage account create](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/account#az-storage-account-create).

## Create a container

Next, create a container in your storage account to hold the boxes:

```shell-session
$ az storage container create --name CONTAINER_NAME --account-name ACCOUNT_NAME
```

For more options, refer to
[az storage container create](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/container#az-storage-container-create).

## Upload a box

With the container ready, upload a box into it. Use `--name` to set the blob path
within the container and `--file` to point to the local `vagrant.box` file:

```shell-session
$ az storage blob upload --account-name ACCOUNT_NAME --container-name CONTAINER_NAME --name NAME --file PATH_TO_BOX
```

For example, a `--name` like `BOX_NAME/VERSION/PROVIDER/ARCHITECTURE/vagrant.box`
keeps your boxes organized by version, provider, and architecture. For more upload
options, refer to
[az storage blob upload](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/blob#az-storage-blob-upload).

## Make the container public

Containers are private by default. To let Vagrant download boxes without
authentication, you need to open up public access at two levels: on the storage
account, and then on the container within it.

Start by allowing public access at the storage account level:

```shell-session
$ az storage account update --name ACCOUNT_NAME --resource-group GROUP_NAME --allow-blob-public-access true
```

With that enabled, set the container's public access level to `blob`. This grants
public read access to individual blobs while keeping the container listing
private:

```shell-session
$ az storage container set-permission --name CONTAINER_NAME --account-name ACCOUNT_NAME --public-access blob
```

For more details, refer to
[az storage container set-permission](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/container#az-storage-container-set-permission).

~> **Warning:** A public container allows anyone to download its blobs. Only make
a container public if the boxes it contains are safe to distribute publicly. Every
public download also incurs data transfer charges on your account, so a widely
shared or high-traffic box can lead to unexpected costs.

## Reference a box from a public container

For a public container, the blob link has the following form:

```text
https://STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME.blob.core.windows.net/CONTAINER_NAME/NAME
```

Reference the box in your Vagrantfile with `config.vm.box_url`:

```ruby
Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  config.vm.box = "BOX_NAME"
  config.vm.box_url = "AZURE_BLOB_URL"
end
```

## Reference a box from a private container

When a container is private, its blobs are not available at a public URL, so you
download the box first and add it to Vagrant locally.

Download the box blob from the container, passing the blob's `--name` and the
local file name to save it as:

```shell-session
$ az storage blob download --account-name ACCOUNT_NAME --container-name CONTAINER_NAME --name NAME --file LOCAL_FILE
```

For more download options, refer to
[az storage blob download](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/storage/blob#az-storage-blob-download).

Add the downloaded box to Vagrant under a name of your choice:

```shell-session
$ vagrant box add BOX_NAME LOCATION
```

`LOCATION` is the path to the box file you downloaded in the previous step. For
more options, refer to
[vagrant box add](/vagrant/docs/cli/box#box-add).

After you add the box, reference it directly in your Vagrantfile by name:

```ruby
Vagrant.configure("2") do |config|
  config.vm.box = "BOX_NAME"
end
```
